evidence: Current native library paginates files, at most100 per page. Grouping only those loaded files can split one broadcast across pages and misstate its file count or bytes.

Current frontend refresh merges the first page into retained older pages. It cannot remove externally deleted older rows or correctly reconcile groups whose latest completion moves across the cursor boundary.

CHZZK independently groups its complete catalog before paging24groups, overlays multiple-file expansion, preserves explicit closed states and filters selection to visible files. Its empty detail placeholder is not a fake selected card or an instruction to create a new detail pane for every platform.
identity: Only completed live recordings with receiver-verified broadcastId can share a group. YouTube key includes provider/live/broadcastId. SOOP additionally includes canonical channel identity. No title/date/profile/channel-only grouping or remote backfill.
Live recordings without verified identity form individual libraryId groups. VOD remains an individual card even if repeated downloads have the same external ID.
Native-generated versioned opaque group keys are stable across title, member-count, representative and presentation changes. Caller group keys are validated lookup keys, never filesystem paths.
readModel: Add a group-summary page API and an independently paginated group-member API. Keep existing flat library and per-file open/delete/profile/thumbnail APIs compatible. No new database, persistent catalog snapshots, receiver or media mutation.

A summary uses the entire provider catalog for fileCount/totalBytes/latest representative, then pages by latestCompletedAt descending plus stable key. It must never claim the first100files are the whole group. VOD entries carry their individual item.

Group cursors bind provider, version, catalogRevision and ordering boundary. Member cursors bind provider, group key, membership revision and ordering boundary. Use strict schemas, validated identifiers, bounded input and1..100 output items. New group/member cursors may use a separate512byte cap; the compatible flat API retains256bytes.

Revisions are deterministic digests of the relevant complete metadata, not process-local random HashMap iteration order. No disk reads or remote requests while holding the media-state lock. Avoid cloning all media DTOs merely to return one page; assess scan cost on large synthetic catalogs.

Changed revisions return a typed catalog_changed/group_changed result, never silently continue a stale cursor or report an empty successful result. Invalid or cross-provider cursors remain explicit errors. A group's first member page returns a fresh summary and its members from the same locked metadata snapshot; the client atomically adopts both only after all requested pages match that membership revision, never mixes a previously displayed135-file summary with a134-file result. Missing last-member groups return a typed missing result and are reconciled without inventing an empty successful group.

Stored per-file chat warnings remain on actual file cards. Group summaries must not label all members healthy based only on their representative, nor inspect unlimited member files on every poll. Sidecar warnings can change without catalog or membership revisions: retain explicit bounded status refresh for the open group's loaded pages even when metadata revision is unchanged, with no overlapping polling and late-response rejection. Each native page reads at most100 selected file statuses outside the state lock. Do not conflate metadata revision stability with unchanged chat preservation.
frontend: Keep current VOD cards and their interaction unchanged. Recording group cards keep cover/profile/channel/title/file information with a fixed-position disclosure and actual complete file count. Opening a group does not select or delete all its files.

Group files open in an overlay with internal bounded scrolling rather than pushing other cards. At most one multi-file overlay is foregrounded. A loading indicator, concise error/retry and loaded-count/total-count accompany member pagination.

All groups can be closed; never force the first group open. Persist one provider-scoped versioned openKey or explicit null/no-open state, rather than a map that could later reopen unloaded groups. Do not erase retained state merely because initial loading or the first page omits its group. Opening B replaces a stored later-page A even before A has loaded; closing B persists null.

Interpret the original empty-space requirement as stable card/list minimum geometry in this library, which has no existing side detail pane. Do not add a new empty detail pane or fabricate selection. This is a recorded adaptation, not exact reproduction of CHZZK's separate detail column.

Selection consists only of visible VOD cards and loaded files in expanded groups. Use the independent platform mediaSelection helper. Closing a group or replacing/removing its files prunes hidden IDs and anchors. Ctrl+A never includes unrequested or hidden members. Group headings consume their own click/double-click/context events.

Polling must remain single-flight. If the catalog revision is unchanged, skip reloading older pages. Otherwise fetch the already displayed N summary pages at one revision into a staging buffer and atomically replace the list. A second revision change defers to a later poll or explicit retry, not an unbounded recursive retry loop; retain the prior visible list with honest refresh state.

Expanded member pages reconcile at their own membership revision, independently of unrelated groups. Query epochs reject late responses after provider/expansion changes, deletion or replacement. Deleting uses actual selected libraryId/revision, never a broad group key.

Refresh, sorting, expansion and selection pruning must not change playback token/video node. Context menu, confirmation and player keyboard priority, privacy masking, stable toggle geometry and reduced-motion behavior remain intact.

wireContract.firstMemberPage: The first cursor-null response is a current coherent group+members snapshot, not bound to an earlier summary. Frontend atomically updates that group's summary and its staged member pages only when all pages share the returned groupRevision. Later cursor mismatch is typed changed. No silent old/new count mixture.
